title: Quantifying Privacy: The Delta-Presence Metric
description: The delta-presence privacy metric is a quantitative measure of the privacy of a dataset that evaluates the difference in the amount of information that can be inferred about an individual before and after their data is removed, but it has limitations such as assuming the dataset is static and not accounting for re-identification attacks.

title: GDPR Compliance: Protecting Personal Data
description: The General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) is a privacy act implemented by the European Union (EU) in May 2018 to protect the personal data of EU citizens and residents by regulating how organizations collect, process, and store their data. Organizations that fail to comply with the GDPR can face significant fines of up to �20 million or 4% of their global annual revenue, whichever is higher. To comply with GDPR, organizations must appoint a Data Protection Officer (DPO), conduct a data audit, obtain consent from individuals, implement appropriate technical and organizational measures, provide individuals with the right to access, correct, and delete their data, report data breaches, and ensure that third-party processors comply with GDPR requirements.

title: Title: "Homomorphic Encryption: Revolutionizing Data Privacy"

title: Protecting Privacy with T Closeness Algorithm
description: The T Closeness Algorithm is a privacy-preserving data anonymization technique that ensures the distribution of sensitive attributes in a dataset is similar to their distribution in the overall population, making it a good choice for sharing data with third parties while protecting individual privacy. However, it has some limitations, including the need for a large dataset, potential for information loss, and vulnerability to re-identification attacks.
